cards.front: What is the core difference between jugar and practicar?
cards.back:
jugar al / a la [sport] = to play a sport (a game, a match)
practicar [sport] = to practice or engage in a sport (as a hobby/activity)
cards.grammarNote: Use jugar when emphasizing playing an actual game. Use practicar when talking about doing the sport as a regular activity or practicing skills.

cards.back:
jugar + a + definite article + sport

jugar al fútbol
jugar al píckleball
jugar al tenis
jugar a la pelota
cards.grammarNote: jugar always takes 'a' before the sport. 'a + el' contracts to 'al'. Feminine sports use 'a la'.

cards.back:
practicar + (definite article) + sport

practicar el tenis
practicar el senderismo
practicar el ciclismo
practicar píckleball
cards.grammarNote: practicar does NOT use 'a'. The article is optional with practicar — both 'practicar tenis' and 'practicar el tenis' are correct.

cards.back:
yo juego
tú juegas
él/ella/usted juega
nosotros jugamos
vosotros jugáis
ellos/ustedes juegan
cards.grammarNote: jugar is irregular: the 'u' stem changes to 'ue' in all forms except nosotros and vosotros.

cards.back:
yo practico
tú practicas
él/ella/usted practica
nosotros practicamos
vosotros practicáis
ellos/ustedes practican
cards.grammarNote: practicar is regular in the present tense. Note the spelling change c→qu in the yo preterite: practiqué.

cards.back: Jeffrey juega al píckleball todos los sábados.
cards.grammarNote: Use jugar al because this refers to actually playing the game on Saturdays.

cards.front: Jeffrey practices pickleball to improve his serve.
cards.back: Jeffrey practica el píckleball para mejorar su saque.
cards.grammarNote: Use practicar because the focus is on the activity of practicing (drilling skills), not a specific game.

cards.front: Do you want to play tennis with me?
cards.grammarNote: jugar al tenis = playing a game of tennis together. The question is an invitation to play.

cards.front: She practices swimming three times a week.
cards.back: Ella practica la natación tres veces a la semana.
cards.grammarNote: Swimming (la natación) is an activity she does regularly — practicar is the right choice here.

cards.front: My brothers and I played basketball yesterday.
cards.back: Mis hermanos y yo jugamos al baloncesto ayer.
cards.grammarNote: A completed game in the past with 'ayer' — jugar is appropriate. Note nosotros preterite = jugamos.

cards.front: Which activities use ONLY practicar (not jugar)?
cards.back:
practicar el senderismo (hiking)
practicar el ciclismo (cycling)
practicar la natación (swimming)
practicar el atletismo (athletics)
practicar yoga
cards.grammarNote: Activities that are not 'games' with opposing players do not use jugar. You cannot say 'jugar al senderismo'.

cards.front: Fill in the blank: Yo ___ al píckleball con mis hermanos.
cards.back:
Yo juego al píckleball con mis hermanos.
(I play pickleball with my brothers.)
cards.grammarNote: jugar al is required — this is an actual game being played with people.

cards.front: Fill in the blank: Ella ___ el tenis en el club.
cards.back:
Ella practica el tenis en el club.
(She practices tennis at the club.)

OR: Ella juega al tenis en el club.
(She plays tennis at the club.)

Both are correct depending on context.
cards.grammarNote: Either verb works here. Practicar emphasizes skill development; jugar emphasizes the game itself.

cards.front: Can jugar mean anything besides sports?
cards.back:
Yes! jugar also means 'to play' in a general sense:

jugar a las cartas — to play cards
jugar un papel — to play a role
jugar con fuego — to play with fire (idiom)
jugar videojuegos — to play video games
cards.grammarNote: jugar is the general verb for 'to play'. Note: jugar videojuegos does NOT use 'a' because videojuegos is not preceded by an article.

cards.back:
JUGAR AL / A LA
+ Implies a game or match
+ Needs 'a + article'
+ Stem-changing (u→ue)

PRACTICAR
+ Implies activity, hobby, or drilling
+ No preposition 'a'
+ Regular -ar verb
cards.grammarNote: When in doubt: if you can say 'play a game of ___', use jugar. If you can say 'do ___ as a sport', use practicar.
